fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline nanowire/MD system does not reconstruct the homogenized [1̄23]-oriented bulk FCC single-crystal compression study.

It attributes cryogenic behavior primarily to twinning, FCC-HCP transformation, and cross-section reorientation rather than thermally activated dislocation glide, MSAD-controlled solid-solution resistance, and phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling.
The cited cross-section reorientation evidence principally concerns Ag nanowires and does not establish that this mechanism produces the claimed HEA response.
The hypothesis omits the elevated-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier regime and its Mn/Fe-dependent Cottrell-type solute pinning.
explanation: The response identifies the related equiatomic CoNiCrFeMn alloy family and addresses cryogenic plasticity, so it is a literature-supported alternative to the target rather than wholly unsupported. However, nearly every defining feature of the hidden study is absent or replaced: nanowires and MD instead of bulk oriented single-crystal compression, an Ag comparison instead of compositionally related concentrated alloys, and strength–ductility instead of temperature-dependent CRSS. It also lacks the 9–1373 K range, strain-rate jumps, TEM/DFT tests, inertial low-temperature crossover, MSAD scaling, and high-temperature serrated PL strengthening. The proposed falsification test can compare overall mechanical performance but cannot discriminate the asserted twinning/transformation synergy from alternative mechanisms.
